name: LBNL 2014 US PUE by space type - localized: 2.0 (component sum: 1 | 0.05 | 0.2 | 0.73 | 0.02 -> IT 1, transformer 0.05, UPS 0.20, cooling 0.73, lighting 0.02)
unit: PUE ratio (total facility energy / IT equipment energy), 2014 baseline
methodology: MODELED BASELINE, TABLE 4 ('2014 PUE by Space Type') of the DOE/BL United States Data Center Energy Usage Report. The row decomposes total PUE into IT (=1 by definition), transformer, UPS, cooling and lighting contributions, and the components sum to the stated total - which is how the table was verified here rather than trusted. Space types are IDC-defined and span both internal enterprise spaces and service-provider spaces; the report states service provider data centers are INCLUSIVE of colocation facilities. This is the most granular public per-facility-type PUE breakdown available from an authoritative US government source. engine_id is ollama only as a schema placeholder: facility metric, no engine.
notes: Localized: back to closet-class efficiency once real cooling capacity exists. Same 2.0 as closet but reached by a different component split (cooling 0.73 rather than UPS 0.93), which is the evidence that the difference between a good and bad small site is UPS topology, not cooling. CAVEAT ON AGE: these are 2014 values and the 2016 report frames the 2020 trajectory separately (dynamic range, consolidation). For a current planning number prefer the 2025 Update's 1.45 national all-equipment average. The 2014 table is retained because the modern public sources publish only fleet or national AVERAGES - this table is the only public breakdown that shows a colocation-class facility is closer to 1.9 than to 1.2.
